candidate_relations.reason: Atypical intravascular cells that are GATA3-positive after breast cancer are metastatic carcinoma, not cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
Postradiation angiosarcoma is the key vascular-malignancy differential; tumor cells are GATA3-positive carcinoma within CD31-positive vessels, i.e., TMBC not angiosarcoma.
Angiosarcoma would label the malignant cells as endothelial; here endothelium is CD31-positive and the atypical cells are GATA3-positive carcinoma.
Kaposi sarcoma is an HHV8 vascular tumor, not metastatic breast carcinoma.
Telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma matches the reference TMBC.
Telangiectasia is the clinical vascular appearance, not the metastatic carcinoma.
Angiosarcoma of the skin is the same incompatible endothelial malignancy.
Stewart-Treves is post-mastectomy lymphangiosarcoma of a lymphedematous arm, not facial telangiectatic metastasis.
Basal cell carcinoma is a primary keratinocytic tumor.
Cutaneous angiosarcoma remains the principal conflicting vascular sarcoma.
Squamous cell carcinoma is a different epithelial tumor.
Lymphoma is a lymphoid malignancy, not GATA3-positive carcinoma.
Cutaneous metastasis is the parent process without telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: cutaneous metastasis missing telangiectatic breast carcinoma
